name: Fatemonger
flavor: Luck is a resource like any other. It belongs to whoever is paying attention, and nobody in this company pays attention like you.

features.name: Loaded Odds
features.description: Once on each of your turns, when an ally you can see within 30 feet rolls a 1 on a d20 for an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, you can use no action to make them reroll it. They must use the new roll.
features.sheetSummary: No action, 1/turn, 30 ft. When an ally rolls a 1 on a d20 for an attack, check, or save, they reroll and must use the new result.
features.narration: You see it come up and you simply refuse it — a click of the tongue, a flick of the wrist — and the moment rewinds half a second into something survivable.

features.name: The House Always Collects
features.description: Fortune runs both ways at your table. When a creature within 30 feet that you can see rolls a natural 20 on an attack roll against one of your allies, you gain 1 Mirth — the worse it gets, the better your material.
features.sheetSummary: Gain 1 Mirth whenever a creature within 30 ft rolls a natural 20 on an attack roll against one of your allies.
features.narration: The worst possible thing happens and you laugh first, because a disaster is just a setup with better timing, and you have already worked out what it is setting up.

features.name: Never Pays to Bet Against Him
features.description: You have an unnatural nose for a wager. You know instinctively whether a game of chance, a contract, or an offer put to you is rigged, though not how. Once per long rest, when you make a bet, a bargain, or a wager of any kind and lose, you may declare that you meant to — you recover whatever you staked, and everyone present remembers it as a joke you were making.
features.sheetSummary: You instinctively know whether a game, contract, or offer is rigged, but not how. Once per long rest, when you lose a bet or bargain, declare you meant to: you recover your stake and everyone remembers it as a joke.
features.narration: You lose spectacularly, take a bow for it, and by the time the laugh dies down the money is back in your hand and nobody can reconstruct how the bet was ever serious.
